clue.text: Tailless elephant went in front having been put in the wrong order

definitions.text: having been put in the wrong order

indicators.note: an animal without its tail loses its final letter, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: Jumbo was a famous elephant, and the name is a byword for one
to have gone in front is to have led

explanation.surface: A bob-tailed elephant marches at the head of a parade that has got out of sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Things muddled out of sequence are said to be mixed up in a disordered heap.

clue.text: Jack with a French city girl

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A man named Jack goes off to the Riviera with a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so an example of a female first name.

clue.text: Reason to go about half-time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for going is placed around the other piece

parts.note: to go is to move

indicators.note: half of the word time is just its opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: A football manager's reason for leaving the pitch at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' looks like the interval in a football match, but it splits into the selection signal 'half' and the word 'time', while 'about' wraps the going word around that piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the cause or ground that prompts someone to act.

clue.text: Ground that had been secured was cut off from the sea

parts.note: ground means land, the earth underfoot
something secured with a key has been locked

explanation.surface: A plot of land that had been fenced off was separated from the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A country with no coastline is enclosed entirely by other territory.

clue.text: Fresh flower?

parts.note: the idiom 'as fresh as a' certain small white meadow bloom, so the flower famed for freshness

explanation.surface: A florist asks whether a bloom has just been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The common expression 'fresh as a daisy' links this meadow bloom with being lively and refreshed.

clue.text: Leading trombonist in e scale performed using another instrument

indicators.note: the leading letter of trombonist is put inside the rearranged scale letters
a piece performed is worked over, so the letters of e scale are rearranged
leading picks the first letter of trombonist

explanation.surface: The principal trombone player plays the scale of E on a different instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' rearranges E SCALE to CELESA, and 'in' puts T (first letter of trombonist, picked by 'Leading') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, giving a bell-like sound.

clue.text: Drink up endlessly grounds first from percolator

indicators.note: first says the grounds piece comes before the drink piece

parts.note: coffee grounds, so grounds suggests coffee

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Someone drinks up and empties the grounds out of the percolator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' looks like the stuff thrown away, but it points to the beverage; 'endlessly' trims the drinking word and 'up' turns what is left, while 'first' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A percolator is a type of brewing vessel for making the hot beverage from beans.

clue.text: Bumpkin not in lake first

indicators.note: first places the lake abbreviation at the front

parts.note: L is a common map abbreviation for lake
not in means out, away from home

explanation.surface: A country yokel is the first to be absent from the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpkin is an uncouth person, a boorish oaf.

clue.text: One in France getting in very small amount of illumination during the day

indicators.note: getting in means the French word for one enters the other word

parts.note: a slight is a very small amount, as in not the slightest
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A French visitor enjoys a little daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Daytime illumination comes from the sun's rays.

clue.text: Space with set of rules for dialling prefix

parts.note: a space is an area
a code is a set of rules, as in highway code

explanation.surface: A room has instructions for making telephone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone number begins with digits identifying its geographic zone.

clue.text: Off!

parts.note: an exclamation of protest, meaning that behaviour is unacceptable, as an indignant person would say of rude conduct

explanation.surface: A shout of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying conduct is 'off' means it is unacceptable, out of order.

clue.text: Special advantage having power to sway other people's thinking

definitions.meaning: pull or clout, the advantage of having connections

definitions.text: power to sway other people's thinking
definitions.meaning: the capacity to affect what others believe or do

explanation.surface: A privileged person has sway over the opinions of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout gives a person leverage, and the same noun covers persuading others' views.

clue.text: Soldiers, fellows getting behind the troop

indicators.note: getting behind means the fellows piece follows the troop piece

parts.note: the cavalry is the mounted troop of an army
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Soldiers and their comrades bring up the rear of the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounted soldiers who serve in a horse regiment.

clue.text: Is in current hit parade perhaps

indicators.note: in places the word is inside the abbreviation for current

parts.note: DC is direct current
taken as written

explanation.surface: A song is currently in the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A record is what appears in a chart of popular music, so a hit parade entry.

clue.text: From Beirut Joe and I removed jewellery

indicators.note: removed means moved about, so the letters of Beirut, Joe and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: Joe and I took some jewellery out of Beirut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' reads as taking things away but is the anagram signal: re-moved, moved again.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived word for trinkets and small ornaments collectively.

clue.text: Did — skilfully

definitions.meaning: did means achieved or carried out
done with skill; the adjective describes someone who acts skilfully

explanation.surface: Someone did a job with real skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is an adverb while the answer works as an adjective, a looseness typical of this kind of clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of achieve covers 'did', and the adjective means talented or expert.

clue.text: Attack on something funny in street

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the funny thing inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a laugh is something funny, as in it was a laugh

explanation.surface: An assault on a comedian in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce assault or onrush by an attacking force.

clue.text: An iron when it's in the same place for too long on a very hot day

definitions.text: An iron when it's in the same place for too long
definitions.meaning: an iron left still burns the cloth, so it becomes a thing that singes

explanation.surface: Ironing left unattended during a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that singes, and a colloquial word for a blistering summer day.

clue.text: Physicist potentially strong entering before noon

indicators.note: entering means the rearranged letters go into the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

indicators.note: potentially suggests what the letters of strong could become when rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist might well arrive in strong form in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges the six letters of strong, and 'entering' puts them inside the morning abbreviation; the scientist is Anders Ångström.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Ångström was a Swedish scientist, after whom a tiny unit of length is named.

clue.text: Voices rant on disrupting dialogue

indicators.note: disrupting breaks up the order of the letters in the phrase voices rant on

explanation.surface: Raised voices ranting on break up a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A talk between two or more people.

clue.text: Musical ice-cream?

definitions.meaning: a brass instrument like a small trumpet
a cone of wafer filled with ice cream

explanation.surface: Someone asks about an ice cream with a musical theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a brass instrument and a wafer cone for a frozen dessert.

clue.text: Joint stake

parts.note: a stake, a pointed rod, pushed through a joint of meat for roasting

explanation.surface: A shared investment in a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint stake' reads as a shared financial interest; in fact the joint is meat and the stake is a spit.
explanation.definitionFit: A long metal pin used to hold meat together while it cooks.

clue.text: Plant that was a climber

definitions.meaning: climbed or got up, the past tense of rise

explanation.surface: A plant that used to be a climbing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden shrub with thorny stems, and the past tense of ascending.

clue.text: Sit back lazily and in France toil on interlaced articles

parts.note: to bask is to lie back lazily in the sun
et is French for and
toil means work

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes in France and does a little light craft work.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicker objects woven from interlaced canes or strips.

clue.text: Mark went astray with a Buddhist conception

indicators.note: went astray means the letters of the name Mark wander out of place

explanation.surface: A man called Mark has gone wrong, with a Buddhist idea in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, the principle that one's deeds determine future fate.

clue.text: Only partially advisable to have this on one's passport

indicators.note: only partially means just a part of the word advisable is used

explanation.surface: Advice that it is only partly sensible to carry a stamp in your passport.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry permit stamped or stuck into a travel document.

clue.text: Bring round with her a pioneer

indicators.note: round means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Fetch her and a trailblazer.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner or herald who goes ahead of what is to come.

clue.text: Revive Frenchman before start of Wednesday

parts.note: René is a French man's name

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of Wednesday

explanation.surface: A Frenchman returns to life just before midweek.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore or refresh something, bringing it back to life.

clue.text: Run into some defensive mound

parts.note: to ram is to run into
some means a part of something

explanation.surface: Charging into an earthwork fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthen embankment built around a fort for protection.

clue.text: A reformed assistant?

parts.note: someone reformed is better than before

explanation.surface: A rehabilitated helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' looks like an anagram signal, but it means improved, BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice who helps someone, often in wrongdoing.
